You check whether an answer's factual claims are supported by the exact
context that was actually given to the system that produced the answer.
You do not use any outside knowledge of Formula One. Treat the context
as the only source of truth for this check, even if you believe it is
incomplete or wrong.

You receive a JSON object with:
- "question": the original question text
- "answer": the answer to check
- "context": the literal text that was actually sent to the model that
  produced the answer (for the global mode, this is the reduce step's
  actual input -- the partial answers it was given -- not the original
  corpus and not the final answer's citation_chain).

Step 1: break the answer into its individual factual claims (names,
numbers, dates, stated relationships). Ignore hedges, meta-commentary,
and refusal sentences -- a refusal has zero claims.

Step 2: for each claim, decide:
- "supported": the context directly states or clearly entails this claim.
- "unsupported": the context does not contain this claim and does not
  entail it.
- "unclear": the context is ambiguous or only loosely related -- do not
  use "unclear" as a way to avoid choosing; use it only when a careful
  reading still leaves genuine doubt.

Return only this JSON, nothing else:

{
  "claims": [
    {"claim": "<short paraphrase of the claim>",
     "verdict": "supported" | "unsupported" | "unclear"}
  ],
  "reasoning": "<one or two sentences>"
}

If the answer has no factual claims (e.g. it is a refusal), return an
empty "claims" list.

2009–2012: Unsuccessful title bids and departure from McLaren
During  his  veering  final  years  with  McLaren—a  period  largely  dominated  by  Red  Bull—Hamilton  continued  to  score
podium  finishes  and  race  victories,  and  challenged  for  titles.  Major  technical  regulation  changes  in  2009  led  to  a
challenging  start  for  McLaren.  Often  qualifying  outside  of  the  top  ten,  and  struggling  to  finish  consistently  on  points,
Hamilton's chances of defending his title became unfeasible. Major upgrades at the German Grand Prix saw a dramatic
improvement in performance of the MP4-24 car. From that point onward, Hamilton advanced from eleventh to fifth in the
standings and outscored the rest of the field, securing two race victories and three additional podium finishes across the
remaining nine rounds.

considered Hamilton the best driver of his generation. Following Red Bull and Sebastian Vettel's four-year dominance of
the sport, Hamilton's resolve was tested both professionally and personally as he did not finish higher than fourth in the

for extracting race-winning performances from cars that were not dominant.

Hamilton is regarded as one of the most complete drivers on the grid, excelling across a wide range of areas. He has
been described as having an aggressive driving style, with a natural aptitude for identifying the limits of the car. Mark

(17), which included eleven wins, five second places, and one third place.

to 2006 and from 2010 to 2012. Schumacher won a record-setting seven Formula One World Drivers' Championship
